entities.summary: Virtue, a concept rooted in ancient Greek philosophy, emerged during the Classical era (5th–3rd centuries BCE) as a central idea in ethics and moral inquiry. In Plato's Republic, Socrates discusses the importance of virtue as the highest human good, arguing that it is the source of happiness and fulfillment. Aristotle further develops the concept in his Nicomachean Ethics, defining virtue as a mean between excess and deficiency, and linking it to the development of human character and citizenship. Virtue became a cornerstone of Western philosophical thought, influencing the works of later thinkers such as Cicero, Kant, and Mill, and shaping the foundations of modern moral and political philosophy. Through its enduring impact on Western civilization, virtue has left a lasting legacy in the realms of ethics, politics, and human conduct.
